description: Core rule pack for inaccuracy, completeness, obsolescence, duplication, ownership and identity-theft questions on nationwide consumer reports. Educational summaries only; not legal advice.
disclaimer: CreditOS rule packs summarise publicly available consumer reporting procedures to help the user organise evidence. They are not legal advice and never guarantee any outcome. Accurate negative information is not disputable merely because it is undesirable.

fcra_611.label: FCRA § 611 — Procedure in case of disputed accuracy
fcra_611.summary: A consumer may dispute the completeness or accuracy of an item directly with a consumer reporting agency, which must conduct a reasonable reinvestigation, generally within 30 days (extendable to 45 days when the consumer provides additional relevant information during the period), and must delete or modify information found inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable.

fcra_605.label: FCRA § 605 — Requirements relating to information contained in consumer reports
fcra_605.summary: Most adverse items may not be reported beyond seven years; for delinquent accounts the period runs from 180 days after the date of first delinquency preceding the collection or charge-off. Bankruptcies generally run ten years.

fcra_605b.label: FCRA § 605B — Block of information resulting from identity theft
fcra_605b.summary: With appropriate proof of identity, a copy of an identity theft report, and identification of the information, a consumer reporting agency must block the identified information within four business days, subject to limited exceptions.

fcra_623.label: FCRA § 623 — Responsibilities of furnishers of information
fcra_623.summary: Furnishers must not furnish information they know or have reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate, must correct and update information, must report accounts as disputed when the consumer disputes directly, and must investigate direct disputes submitted under the applicable regulation.

fcra_609.label: FCRA § 609 — Disclosures to consumers
fcra_609.summary: Consumers are entitled to disclosure of the information in their file and the sources of that information upon request.

fdcpa_809.label: FDCPA § 809 — Validation of debts
fdcpa_809.summary: Within the validation period a consumer may dispute a debt in writing and request verification; the collector must cease collection until it obtains and mails verification. Applies to third-party debt collectors.

metro2_dofd.cite: Metro 2® Format — Date of First Delinquency
metro2_dofd.label: Industry reporting standard: DOFD
metro2_dofd.summary: Furnishers report the Date of First Delinquency so that the obsolescence period under FCRA § 605 can be calculated. A missing or shifting DOFD on a delinquent account is a completeness/accuracy question.

rules.title: Balance differs materially across bureaus
rules.description: The same account is reported with different current balances at two or more bureaus. Because furnishers send the same Metro 2 record to each bureau, divergence usually indicates a stale update at one bureau or a furnisher error.
rules.disputableWhen: Report dates are comparable (within ~45 days) and the gap exceeds $50 or 5% of the larger balance; or the user holds a statement contradicting the reported balance.
rules.notDisputableWhen: Report dates are far apart and the difference is plausibly explained by normal payment activity between snapshots.
evidenceRequirements: Two or more bureau snapshots showing the same account key
Report dates for each snapshot
Recent account statement showing the actual balance (optional; raises confidence to high)
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt; up to 45 days if the consumer adds information during the review.

rules.title: Payment status / late history differs across bureaus
rules.description: One bureau shows a delinquency (e.g. 30 days late) that another bureau shows as current for the same month and account.
rules.disputableWhen: The same account and month are reported with conflicting payment statuses, or the user holds proof of on-time payment for the month in question.
rules.notDisputableWhen: All bureaus agree on the delinquency and the user has no proof of timely payment.
evidenceRequirements: Conflicting payment-history entries for the same month across bureaus
Bank/creditor statement or payment confirmation for the disputed month (strongly recommended)
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt; up to 45 days if the consumer adds information during the review.

rules.title: Account status, dates, or limits contradict each other
rules.description: Open vs closed status, opened-date gaps larger than 60 days, or credit limits that disagree for the same account.
rules.disputableWhen: Two bureaus report factually incompatible values for a field that cannot legitimately differ (open date, closed status).
rules.notDisputableWhen: Differences are limited to fields that can lag (e.g. last reported date) or are within normal update windows.
evidenceRequirements: Side-by-side field values with report dates
Account agreement or closing confirmation when status is contested
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Delinquent account reported without a Date of First Delinquency
rules.description: A charged-off, collection, or delinquent account omits the DOFD, which is required to compute when the item must age off the report.
rules.disputableWhen: The account is reported as delinquent, charged off, or in collection and no DOFD is present on the report.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The account is current with no derogatory history.
evidenceRequirements: Snapshot showing derogatory status with DOFD field empty
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Adverse item appears to exceed the reporting period
rules.description: The item's DOFD plus 180 days plus seven years is in the past, yet the item remains on the report.
rules.disputableWhen: A DOFD is present and the computed obsolescence date has passed.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The DOFD is missing (use missing-dofd instead) or the obsolescence date is in the future.
evidenceRequirements: Snapshot showing DOFD and current report date
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Same debt appears twice within one bureau
rules.description: Two tradelines in a single bureau report share the original creditor, balance, and approximate dates — commonly an original creditor and a collector both reporting a balance owed.
rules.disputableWhen: Both tradelines report a balance owed for the same underlying debt.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The original creditor reports a zero balance / transferred status and only the collector reports the balance (this is normal).
evidenceRequirements: Both tradelines from the same snapshot with matching original creditor and amounts
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Hard inquiry the consumer does not recognise
rules.description: A hard inquiry from a subscriber the consumer states they never applied with. Bureaus generally refer inquiry disputes to the subscriber; a direct request to the subscriber for permissible-purpose documentation is often the practical first step.
rules.disputableWhen: The consumer affirmatively states no application was made and no account was opened.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The inquiry corresponds to an application the consumer made, including pre-approvals the consumer accepted.
evidenceRequirements: User statement that no application was made
List of applications made around the inquiry date
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Varies; subscriber responses are not subject to a fixed statutory window.

rules.title: Account the consumer states was opened fraudulently
rules.description: The consumer asserts the account resulted from identity theft. This path requires an identity theft report (e.g. FTC IdentityTheft.gov report or police report) and proof of identity before a block request is appropriate.
rules.disputableWhen: An identity theft report and proof of identity are on file as evidence.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The consumer cannot or will not file an identity theft report; the compliance reviewer must block any letter that asserts identity theft without one.
evidenceRequirements: Identity theft report (FTC or police)
Proof of identity
Identification of the specific items resulting from the theft
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Block within four business days of receipt of a complete request, subject to statutory exceptions.

rules.title: Account ownership / responsibility reported inconsistently
rules.description: One bureau reports the consumer as an individual account holder while another reports authorized user or joint, or the consumer states they were only an authorized user.
rules.disputableWhen: Ownership codes differ across bureaus or contradict account documents.
rules.notDisputableWhen: All bureaus agree and no account document contradicts them.
evidenceRequirements: Conflicting ownership values
Account agreement or card-issuer confirmation of role
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Third-party collection with unclear validation
rules.description: A collection account from a third-party collector where the consumer has not received validation of the debt. A written validation request to the collector is distinct from a bureau accuracy dispute.
rules.disputableWhen: The collector is a third party and the consumer has not received or does not recognise validation details.
rules.notDisputableWhen: The consumer recognises the debt and has already received validation; accuracy questions should be routed through balance/status rules instead.
evidenceRequirements: Collection tradeline details
Any collector correspondence received
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Collector must cease collection until verification is mailed; no fixed response deadline.

rules.title: Previously deleted or corrected item has reappeared
rules.description: An item removed after a prior investigation appears again without the bureau providing the notice required for reinsertion.
rules.disputableWhen: A prior resolution record shows the item was deleted/corrected and a later snapshot shows it again.
rules.notDisputableWhen: No prior resolution record exists in CreditOS or from the bureau.
evidenceRequirements: Prior bureau result letter showing deletion/correction
Later snapshot showing the item again
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Generally 30 days from the bureau's receipt.

rules.title: Accurate isolated late payment — goodwill request only
rules.description: A single accurate late payment on an otherwise positive account. This is not disputable; a goodwill adjustment request to the creditor is the only honest path and is entirely discretionary for the creditor.
rules.disputableWhen: Never — this rule explicitly marks the item as accurate.
rules.notDisputableWhen: Always. Do not route goodwill candidates through bureau disputes.
evidenceRequirements: Account history showing isolated late payment
Explanation of circumstances (user statement)
rules.typicalReviewWindow: Discretionary; creditors are not obligated to respond.

rules.title: Observed change that does not support a dispute
rules.description: A single-bureau tradeline, a new inquiry the user recognises, or a balance change consistent with normal activity. CreditOS records it and keeps watching.
rules.notDisputableWhen: Always; re-evaluate if new evidence arrives.
